styles: Brittle and precise. Corrects the detective's grammar. Hates being interrupted.
Warm and chatty, hiding everything behind friendliness. Volunteers irrelevant detail.
Hostile from the first word. Answers in as few syllables as possible.
Nervous, over-explains, contradicts small details then corrects themselves.
Theatrical. Treats an interrogation as a performance and enjoys it.
Weary and honest-sounding, with one subject they absolutely will not discuss.
Bureaucratic. Answers as if filing a report. Cites procedure constantly.
Gently condescending. Implies the detective is out of their depth.
Grief-stricken and scattered, drifting into memories mid-answer.
Coolly amused. Finds the whole investigation faintly ridiculous.
